programs.name: dzdv
programs.purpose: Estimate the depth derivative with respect to velocity from primary- and extra-amplitude common image gathers.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: DZDV - determine depth derivative with respect to the velocity

params.name: nz
params.description: Number of depth samples per trace.

params.name: fx
params.description: First trace coordinate; the selfdoc calls this required, but the code defaults it.

params.name: fz
params.description: First depth coordinate; the selfdoc calls this required, but the code defaults it.

params.name: nxw
params.description: Horizontal half-width of the least-squares window; capped at nx-1.

params.name: nzw
params.description: Depth half-width of the least-squares window; capped at nz-1.

params.name: cip
params.description: Repeatable x,z,r triples describing common image points; at least one occurrence is required.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Interpolation, sqrt, rounded sample selection, and ordered float least-squares sums affect results. Each cip must contain three values; the code does not validate its length. File-open failures are unchecked.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers two three-dimensional gathers and interpolates and accumulates windowed least-squares estimates.

test_cases.description: Single image point and zero-width windows.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=8 | suop op=exp | sustrip > primary.bin && sunull nt=16 ntr=8 | suop op=exp | sustrip > extra.bin && dzdv nx=4 nz=16 dx=1 dz=1 off0=0 doff=1 noff=2 cip=0,4,0 afile=extra.bin dfile=depth.bin < primary.bin > dzdv.bin

test_cases.description: Interpolate two image points and use nonzero windows.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=8 | suop op=exp | sustrip > primary.bin && sunull nt=16 ntr=8 | suop op=exp | sustrip > extra.bin && dzdv nx=4 nz=16 dx=1 dz=1 fx=0 fz=0 off0=1 doff=1 noff=2 cip=0,4,0.1 cip=3,6,0.2 nxw=1 nzw=2 afile=extra.bin dfile=depth.bin < primary.bin > dzdv.bin

programs.name: rayt2d
programs.purpose: Calculate two-dimensional traveltime tables by paraxial ray tracing, optionally filling shadow zones with an eikonal solver.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: RAYT2D - traveltime Tables calculated by 2D paraxial RAY tracing

params.name: vfile
params.description: Raw-float velocity grid input; omitted means standard input.

params.name: tfile
params.description: Raw-float traveltime output; omitted means standard output.

params.name: aperx
params.description: Tracing aperture; the code adds dxs when nxs>1, including when aperx is supplied.

params.name: restart
params.description: A value starting with y resumes a named tfile.

params.name: jpfile
params.description: Progress-report destination; omitted means standard error.

params.name: pvfile
params.description: Velocity-variation input file, read only when npv is nonzero; the code reads nx*nz floats.

params.name: tvfile
params.description: Traveltime-variation output when npv is nonzero.

params.name: csfile
params.description: Cosine-table output when npv is nonzero.

params.name: surf
params.description: Repeatable recording-surface coordinate pairs in x,z;x,z form.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Runge-Kutta ray integration, cubic interpolation, eikonal updates, trigonometric functions, float/double promotion, and grid-index rounding can change results. Surface strings are copied into a fixed 6144-byte buffer without a length check.
programs.difficulty_reason: It combines dynamic ray integration, spline topography, eikonal updates, optional perturbation tables, and restart state.

test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sugain scale=1500 | sustrip | rayt2d nx=16 nz=16 dx=100 dz=100 fxs=700 nt=101 dt=0.004 na=21 fa=-50 da=5 ek=1 > times.bin

test_cases.description: Sloping surface and velocity-variation outputs without eikonal filling.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sugain scale=1500 | sustrip > velocity.bin && sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sustrip > perturb.bin && rayt2d vfile=velocity.bin nx=16 nz=16 dx=100 dz=100 fxs=700 nt=101 dt=0.004 na=21 fa=-50 da=5 'surf=0,0;1500,100' ek=0 npv=1 pvfile=perturb.bin tvfile=variation.bin csfile=cosines.bin tfile=times.bin

programs.license_note: The header says Dave Hale's modeling-library subroutines were adapted to define topography using cubic splines.

programs.name: rayt2dan
programs.purpose: Trace P or SV rays through a two-dimensional anisotropic medium and calculate traveltime tables.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: RAYT2DAN -- P- and SV-wave raytracing in 2D anisotropic media

params.name: SV
params.description: Select SV waves when 1; default is P waves.

params.name: tfile
params.description: Traveltime output file; omitted means standard output.

params.name: a1111file
params.description: Stiffness input; when absent a1111 is set to VP0 squared.

params.name: a1133file
params.description: Stiffness input; when absent a1133 is set to 0.4 times VP0 squared.

params.name: VS0file
params.description: Vertical S-wave velocity input; when absent VS0 is set to 0.5477 times VP0.

params.name: a1113file
params.description: Stiffness input; when absent its values are zero.

params.name: a3313file
params.description: Stiffness input; when absent its values are zero.

params.name: deltafile
params.description: Thomsen delta input; absent values are zero when Thomsen parameters are used.

params.name: epsilonfile
params.description: Thomsen epsilon input; absent values are zero when Thomsen parameters are used.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Anisotropic ray integration, stiffness calculations, interpolation, square roots, trigonometric functions, and float/double mixing are sensitive to rounding. The program copies nt ray steps even when the ray terminates early, so uninitialized steps may be read. It prints source and angle text to stdout even when binary tables also go there.
programs.difficulty_reason: It implements anisotropic dynamic ray tracing and interpolation with multiple stiffness and wave-mode paths.

test_cases.description: P-wave tracing in a constant isotropic model, with binary output sent to a named file.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sugain scale=1500 | sustrip > velocity.bin && rayt2dan VP0file=velocity.bin nx=16 nz=16 nt=101 dt=0.004 dx=100 dz=100 fsx=700 na=11 fa=-50 da=10 tfile=times.bin

test_cases.description: SV tracing with supplied Thomsen parameter grids.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sugain scale=1500 | sustrip > velocity.bin && sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | sustrip > anisotropy.bin && rayt2dan VP0file=velocity.bin deltafile=anisotropy.bin epsilonfile=anisotropy.bin nx=16 nz=16 nt=101 dt=0.004 dx=100 dz=100 fsx=700 SV=1 na=11 fa=-50 da=10 tfile=times.bin

programs.name: wkbj
programs.purpose: Calculate first-arrival traveltimes and WKBJ ray quantities by finite differences on a velocity grid.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: WKBJ - Compute WKBJ ray theoretic parameters, via finite differencing
programs.float_sensitive_notes: The eiktam finite-difference solver uses ordered numerical updates and floating-point math; its results depend on rounding. The input fread result is unchecked, so a short velocity input leaves values uninitialized.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program delegates its core work to a finite-difference eikonal and transport solver.

test_cases.description: Constant velocity with a centered surface source.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sugain scale=1500 | sustrip | wkbj nx=16 nz=16 xs=700 zs=0 dx=100 dz=100 sfile=sigma.bin bfile=beta.bin afile=angle.bin > times.bin

test_cases.description: Off-center source and nonzero grid origins.
test_cases.command: sunull nt=16 ntr=16 | suop op=exp | sugain scale=2000 | sustrip | wkbj nx=16 nz=16 fx=100 fz=50 dx=50 dz=50 xs=350 zs=150 sfile=sigma.bin bfile=beta.bin afile=angle.bin > times.bin
